subQuestions.questionText:
Various options are provided as possible answers. Choose the correct answer and write only the letter (A–D) next to the question number.

A study strategy that could help you to study effectively could include ...
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C — studying over a longer period of time. (1)

Spreading studying over a longer period (distributed practice) is more effective than cramming into a short period.

options.A: studying within a short period of time.
options.C: studying over a longer period of time.

subQuestions.questionText: The Labour Relations Act (LRA), 1995 (Act 66 of 1995) allows for the dismissal of workers based on ...
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D — a worker's general performance. (1)

The LRA permits fair dismissal on grounds of conduct, capacity (performance) or operational requirements — not on redress, affirmative action or gender.

subQuestions.questionText: An example of embezzlement could be ...
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A — using the company's resources for personal gain. (1)

Embezzlement is the theft or misappropriation of funds/resources placed in one's trust, such as a company's resources used for personal gain.

options.A: using the company's resources for personal gain.
options.B: awarding a contract without following procedures.
options.C: accepting a payoff to give someone access to theft.
options.D: demanding a reward from a contracted supplier.

subQuestions.questionText: To discuss an issue in an examination question paper means to ...
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C — demonstrate your reasoning skills. (1)

To 'discuss' means to present and reason through different points/arguments, showing your reasoning, rather than to estimate importance, show connections or define.

options.D: give the precise meaning of concepts.

subQuestions.questionText: The government has a duty to lawfully restrict freedom of expression to some extent ...
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B — for reasons of public principles. (1)

Freedom of expression may be lawfully limited in the public interest (e.g. to prevent hate speech, incitement to violence or propaganda for war).
subQuestions.topic: Democracy, human rights and the media

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.

Shared beliefs, customs, activities, traditions, values, religions and ideas that are common to a particular group or society.
subQuestions.memoText: Culture / cultural practices. (1)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.

A strong sense of suitability to follow a particular career, job, profession or occupation.
subQuestions.memoText: Vocation / calling. (1)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.

The act of using technology to intentionally harass or intimidate someone by sending messages of a threatening nature.

subQuestions.questionText:
Answer in full sentences.

State TWO benefits of managing stress appropriately, which could improve your quality of life.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award ONE mark for each of TWO responses. Any TWO of:
• Experience better physical and emotional health.
• Have a better chance of achieving your goals.
• Build and sustain healthier relationships.
• Avoid psychological problems.
• Become a happier person and live a less stressful, more carefree life with less worry and anxiety.
• Make better, more rational decisions and stay more focused.
• Gain more self-confidence.
• Become more successful at daily tasks.
• Reduce stress hormones.
• Enhance your self-esteem.
• Prevent you from becoming depressed.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the term nation building.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks for a well-explained response. It may refer to any ONE of:
• People of a country coming or working together and being united to achieve a common goal or support national teams and nation-building initiatives.
• A shared sense of community among a population.
• An ongoing process of developing a shared sense of national identity.
• The development of relations between citizens and their state.
• A process whereby individuals and groups interact to establish social relations.
• A process of nurturing a sense of community among citizens where none previously existed or where it was undermined by internal conflict.
• An ongoing process aimed at establishing an integrated society based on shared values and goals.
• A sense of unity and cohesion within a country.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss ONE benefit of scanning as a reading skill.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks for a well-explained response. It may help you to:
• Quickly find specific information, saving time when searching for particular data.
• Reduce reading time / swiftly identify specific data or figures / speedily determine which parts of notes or content to use, so you have enough time to complete a task.
• Easily find key words within a text, which assists in understanding a specific idea.
• Improve your reading skills, making your reading process more efficient.
(1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.passageText:
ADAPTING TO GROWTH AND CHANGE IN A GLOBALISED WORLD

Young people today live in a dynamic and globalised world where change is inevitable. Therefore, they need to prepare themselves for an inclusive global and sustainable world of work.

Glossary: globalised — ideas, knowledge, information, goods and services spread around the world; global — worldwide/international; sustainable — to continue over a period of time.

[Adapted from www.qs-gen.com. Accessed on 03/01/2023.]
subQuestions.questionText:
Read the source above and answer the question. Write your answers in full sentences.

Explain what it means to adapt to changes in social circumstances.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks for a well-explained response. It means that you may have to:
• Interact with new people or cultures and make new friends, which helps you cope with your new circumstances and feel less isolated.
• Get used to new ways of thinking and doing things so you fit into new social circles more easily.
• Develop the necessary social skills to face new challenges as they arise.
• Learn different ways to deal with new or unfamiliar social responsibilities.
• Become more suitable for a new role or purpose in different social settings.
• Make adjustments according to changing social environments.
(1 x 2) (2)
subQuestions.topic: Adapting to growth and change in a globalised world

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss ONE advantage of living in a globalised world for your career development.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks for a well-explained response. It may offer you any ONE of:
• Opportunities for lifelong learning, since you have access to worldwide platforms and institutions of learning.
• Increased employment possibilities, since globalisation brings increased career options.
• International networking opportunities, leading to new and valuable business connections.
• A broader understanding of different ways of thinking, giving you a better perception of today's global economy.
• Valuable multicultural experiences on an international level, which are highly valued by employers.
• The ability to transition from one type of work to another, since it is easier to transfer knowledge and skills between careers.
• The ability to work from anywhere in the world, due to constant advancements in technology.
• Easy access to global markets, making you more skilled in international business affairs.
• The ability to go beyond your immediate geographic location, greatly increasing your professional networks.
• The chance to develop highly sought-after skills, helping you stay ahead of the curve in your industry.
(1 x 2) (2)
subQuestions.topic: Adapting to growth and change in a globalised world

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest ONE way in which you could prepare yourself to successfully adapt to global changes in the world of work. Motivate your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks for a well-explained response. You could:
• Constantly look into global developments to stay abreast of what is important to the global job market.
• Continuously upskill yourself technologically so you know how to use digital information on any platform.
• Open yourself up to different perspectives and worldviews and develop strong interpersonal skills to connect positively with others in the global world of work.
• Improve your ability to make reliable judgements so you can effectively assess work-related issues of global concern.
• Build work relationships with peers and professionals globally in your field, since they can offer guidance, support and valuable insights.
• Learn to question information critically, which helps you make better-informed decisions in global work settings.
• Learn foreign languages to communicate more effectively with people from different international backgrounds.
• Look for opportunities to gain diverse practical skills you can apply in a variety of work contexts.
• Be willing and open to learn new things and explore new ideas, developing a more flexible, adaptable mindset.
• Develop a growth mindset so you stay motivated under challenging circumstances in a global work environment.
• Become more sensitive to global intercultural matters, helping you understand how you fit into the global work community and ensuring respectful interactions.
(1 x 2) (2)
subQuestions.topic: Adapting to growth and change in a globalised world

questions.title: SECTION B (Compulsory) — Question 2: Long-term engagement in physical activity (Preventing lifestyle diseases)
questions.passageText:
LONG-TERM ENGAGEMENT IN PHYSICAL ACTIVITY — Preventing lifestyle diseases

Being physically inactive has proven to be one of the major health challenges globally, leading to lifestyle diseases. Despite the facts about the benefits of being physically active, an inactive lifestyle and its negative consequences remain a concern worldwide.

Research has shown that being physically active could increase your energy levels. It could also aid in preventing lifestyle diseases and prevent people from turning to harmful substances when confronted with difficulties in life.

Recent research in South Africa has also found that a variety of factors could influence people's participation in physical activities. These include intrapersonal, interpersonal, environmental and social factors.

Committing to an action plan could assist in ensuring that you improve your health; however, having a proper plan of action is important.

[Adapted from www.openpublichealthjournal.com. Accessed on 02/01/2023.]

subQuestions.questionText: Define the term lifestyle diseases. (No marks are awarded for examples.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks for a well-explained response. Any ONE of:
• Illnesses caused by people's way of life that could lead to chronic conditions.
• Ailments caused by the day-to-day habits of people that pose a threat to their health.
• Diseases linked with the way people live their lives that may be life-threatening.
• Health conditions worsened by aspects of people's lifestyle that impact negatively on their health.
• Diseases that are not transmitted between people but developed over time due to personal lifestyle choices.
• Communicable or non-communicable diseases that develop from unhealthy lifestyle choices.
(1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe ONE way in which being part of a fitness group may motivate you to stay committed to participating in physical activities.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks for a well-explained response. Any ONE of:
• It offers the support you need, helping you stay dedicated to your goal.
• It gives assurance that you are not alone, helping you stay loyal to your pledge and accountable to the group.
• It helps you persevere when you feel like giving up, until exercise becomes a lifestyle.
• It gives a sense of belonging, inspiring you to stay on course.
• It encourages you on the journey, making it easier to stay devoted to your cause.
• You meet people you can relate to, helping you keep participating enthusiastically.
(1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ONE environmental factor that may discourage you from engaging in physical activities.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks for a well-explained response. Any ONE of:
• A high crime rate in your neighbourhood may make you feel unsafe to participate in outdoor activities.
• A lack of amenities (green spaces, parks, trails, outdoor gyms), heavy traffic, noise or unsafe sidewalks could make it difficult to exercise and dampen your interest.
• Living in a community with a culture of no physical activity could negatively influence your attitude towards participating.
• Being raised in a family or traditional environment where being active is not encouraged may deter you from participating.
• Staying far from available facilities could make access costly or unaffordable.
• Unfavourable weather (extreme cold, heat or heavy rain) may make it challenging to be outdoors.
• Air pollution may make you feel at risk of airborne diseases or viruses when doing outdoor activity.
• Land pollution may be hazardous to your health.
(1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss how long-term participation in physical activity could increase your energy levels.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks each for TWO well-explained responses. It may:
• Help you get rid of built-up energy in your body, making you feel less tired.
• Strengthen your body so it has longer-lasting power.
• Enhance bodily functions through improved blood circulation, letting you perform daily tasks more efficiently.
• Strengthen your lungs, increasing stamina and improving endurance.
• Improve your heart rate, helping you perform at a higher level.
• Convert stored energy into active energy, enabling you to function at a faster pace.
• Improve your psychological and mental state, preventing mental and physical fatigue and helping you feel more motivated.
• Help reduce weight and relieve strain on your body, resulting in more sustained energy.
• Release hormones such as dopamine and adrenaline, resulting in more consistent energy levels.
(2 x 2) (4)

subQuestions.questionText: How could being physically active prevent you from turning to harmful substances when you experience difficulties in life?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks each for TWO well-explained responses. It may:
• Provide a healthy outlet for negative emotions and reduce boredom, taking your mind off the temptation to resort to substance abuse.
• Release feel-good hormones that relieve the distress you may be experiencing.
• Reduce the levels of stress hormones in your brain, enabling you to deal better with daunting situations; or lower your stress levels, helping you think more rationally about your situation.
• Give you constructive activities to focus on and a healthy distraction, helping you feel less overwhelmed.
• Help you build healthy social networks that provide the support you need during trying times.
• Help you build physical and mental resilience, so you cope better with stress and adversity.
(2 x 2) (4)

subQuestions.questionText: Assess the importance of proper planning when committing to an action plan to improve your health. In EACH answer, also indicate how it may increase the likelihood of succeeding in your plan.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award THREE marks each for TWO well-explained responses (statement + qualify + outcome). It may:
• Make you aware of factors and risks that could impact your efforts negatively, preparing you for possible hindrances and helping you restructure your activities so you succeed.
• Guide you in taking the necessary actions to achieve your intended goal, keeping you motivated.
• Prepare you to adapt your plan if required, making it easier to follow and ensuring you meet its objectives.
• Alert you to factors that may affect your health, enabling you to align your plan to your health condition for better long-term outcomes.
• Ensure you follow an integrated, holistic approach that considers all aspects influencing your goal, encouraging you to stay engaged.
• Prepare you for possible financial expenses, allowing you to make provision so you can adequately cater for the overall improvement of your health.
• Help you break your target goal into achievable milestones, letting you track progress and measure short-term outcomes.
• Allow you to prioritise your health programme and manage your time efficiently for maximum impact.
• Encourage you to stay accountable and consistent, holding yourself responsible for the results and staying focused on the process.
(2 x 3) (6) [20]

questions.title: SECTION B (Compulsory) — Question 3: South African youth: lack of required skills (Recruitment trends)
questions.passageText:
SOUTH AFRICAN YOUTH: LACK OF REQUIRED SKILLS — Recruitment trends

Most South African post-school youth are still struggling to find suitable jobs, mainly due to a lack of required skills and their inability to keep up with the latest recruitment trends in the job market.

Recruitment trends change over time. The expectations of companies, human resource recruiters and candidates continually change, meaning that one needs to adapt to these changes accordingly.

The most common concern employers have about young job seekers is that they may not realise that they are mainly responsible for risking their chances of getting employed. Employers are also of the opinion that most of the young people that are getting employed need to be more willing to upskill themselves in the job.

Another alarming matter is that young job seekers may not be keeping up with recruitment trends being used by recruiters.

Young job seekers should also realise the importance of having a personal brand, meaning a personal and unique way in which they could market themselves in today's world of work.

[Adapted from https://job-hunt.org. Accessed on 07/01/2023.]

subQuestions.questionText: Define the term recruitment trends. (No marks are awarded for examples.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks for a well-explained response. It may refer to any ONE of:
• Contemporary or modern ways that employers use to source suitably qualified workers.
• Current ways of selecting or placing potential workers, in keeping with the technological advances of the 21st century / Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR).
• Present-day approaches that open up a wider database to recruit candidates whose profile fits particular job requirements.
• The latest methods of identifying and interacting with suitable candidates for a job.
(1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe ONE way in which young job seekers may risk their chances of being considered for an interview.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks for a well-explained response. They may:
• Not follow the requirements in the job advertisement, resulting in disqualification for non-compliance.
• Use a general CV/résumé/portfolio that is not tailored to the specific job requirements.
• Make grammatical or spelling errors in their application documents, indicating a lack of basic academic skills.
• Omit important documents or information, submit forged qualifications or false information, or have a negative social media footprint or criminal record, resulting in them not being invited for an interview.
• Frequently change email addresses or cellphone numbers without informing recruiters, so they miss communication about the outcome.
• Not respond to calls, messages or emails on time or provide alternative contact details, resulting in missed opportunities.
• Not know how to use technology to create or access emails, websites or messages, making them unsuccessful when applying online.
• Use shared email addresses or contact numbers, so they do not receive information about their application.
(1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Why is it important for young workers to continually upskill themselves in a job?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks for a well-explained response. It may enable them to:
• Keep up with new developments related to their job so they can perform their duties accordingly.
• Use the latest equipment so they are familiar with new ways of executing tasks.
• Become more innovative and creative, making them more proficient at their job.
• Develop a deeper understanding of their work, broadening their opportunities for growth and development.
• Use acquired skills to improve their performance, preparing them for promotional posts.
• Stay motivated, since new knowledge and skills make them more confident.
• Enhance their general understanding of workplace operations, keeping them competent.
• Develop a variety of skills, making them more competitive so they are not replaced.
• Discover a new passion through the new knowledge or skills, opening up new job opportunities.
(1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss TWO ways in which you, as a young job seeker, could ensure that you keep up with the latest recruitment trends.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks each for TWO well-explained responses. You could:
• Regularly visit the websites of recruitment agencies and continually research them to stay up to date with new recruitment practices.
• Consult reliable online articles about current recruitment practices to determine common tendencies and what recruiters expect from applicants.
• Have discussions with workers or professionals in your field who have been through the latest recruitment processes, to learn from their experiences.
• Establish networks with recruitment agencies to access the latest information about how recruitment processes have changed.
• Do short online surveys with recruiters to identify common challenges applicants experience.
• Enquire about common recruitment practices from different agencies to understand their specific approach.
• Attend webinars, seminars or conferences related to your field, which expose you to new ideas and emerging recruitment trends.
(2 x 2) (4)

subQuestions.questionText: How could having a personal brand enhance your chances of finding a job?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks each for TWO well-explained responses. It may enable you to:
• Demonstrate in your own way what you are capable of, persuading potential employers that you are the perfect fit.
• Share what you stand for and believe in, showing how your work values align with those of the workplace.
• Express your interests, aptitude and passion personally, highlighting how your unique attributes match the company's vision.
• Showcase your personal achievements in a unique way, convincing the employer of your drive to succeed.
• Reveal your vision for career success, showing how you could contribute to the growth of the organisation.
• Display what motivates you, demonstrating your level of self-motivation.
• Share endorsements, qualifications and achievements on media platforms (LinkedIn, X, TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook), convincing an employer of your suitability.
• Present your distinct skills on various platforms, creating an opportunity for recruiters to notice your rare attributes.
• Establish and maintain an online presence and increase your visibility, improving your chances of being headhunted.
• Create a well-crafted personal brand showing you have authority over your life, making employers view you as more credible and desirable.
(2 x 2) (4)

subQuestions.questionText: Assess TWO advantages of the latest trends in technology used for recruitment processes. In EACH answer, also indicate the benefit for you as a job seeker.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award THREE marks each for TWO well-explained responses (advantage + how it works + benefit to the job seeker). It may:
• Allow interviews to be conducted through online platforms, recruiting candidates across the globe, giving you a fair opportunity to participate, saving on transport costs and being less stressful.
• Speed up recruitment processes, giving candidates feedback within a shorter turnaround time, which lets you consider or accept another job offer.
• Give recruiters access to online platforms candidates use, indicating how candidates conduct themselves, which advantages a job seeker who posts constructive content.
• Offer recruiters access to vast electronic lists of skills, qualifications and experience, making it easier to keep a database of first-choice applicants, giving job seekers multiple opportunities to be considered.
• Ensure a more objective processing of applications, making online recruitment more impartial, so you have a fair chance of being considered based only on job suitability.
• Provide job recommendations through AI-powered search engines that analyse a job seeker's skills, experience and preferences, helping you find positions that match your qualifications and interests.
• Make it easier for job seekers to communicate with employers throughout the hiring process via chatbots and communication platforms, keeping you informed about your application status.
• Allow applicants and people with disabilities to apply online, which is convenient and quicker and reduces the cost and burden of paperwork.
(2 x 3) (6) [20]

questions.title: SECTION C (Answer any TWO of Questions 4, 5 and 6) — Question 4: Human factors causing ill health (Stereotyping as a social factor)
questions.passageText:
SECTION C: Answer any TWO questions in this section. Responses must be in paragraphs; marks are awarded only for responses written in full sentences. If all three questions are answered, only the first TWO are marked.

HUMAN FACTORS CAUSING ILL HEALTH — Stereotyping as a social factor

Stereotyping as a social factor may lead to social classification of others, which is one of the reasons for the 'them' and 'us' attitude that some people may have. Treating people in this way may eventually have a negative impact on the mental health of such victims.

Glossary: stereotyping — often involves judging people based on various factors, without considering their individual qualities and characteristics.

[Adapted from www.simplypsychology.org. Accessed on 04/01/2023.]

Write paragraphs on human factors causing ill health: social factors, using the three points below as a guideline.

subQuestions.questionText: Briefly state FOUR possible social factors that may lead to stereotyping.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award ONE mark for each response. Any FOUR of:
• Gender imbalances or inequalities in society, and racism.
• Ideas learnt about other people from family members, friends or the media.
• Not engaging with people who are different from you in some way.
• Not being open to different ideas or ways of living.
• The media portraying people or a specific gender in a certain way.
• Following the idea that stereotyping is acceptable.
• Being influenced by societal expectations, culture or religion.
• Classifying people according to social class.
(4 x 1) (4)
subQuestions.topic: Human factors causing ill health: social factors

subQuestions.questionText: Analyse TWO negative effects of a social factor, such as stereotyping, on the mental health of victims of stereotyping.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award FOUR marks each for TWO well-explained responses (statement + elaborate + qualify + outcome). Victims of stereotyping may:
• Develop a negative self-concept and low self-esteem, having a negative opinion of themselves, which leads to irrational thinking and false beliefs of worthlessness.
• Experience feelings of despair that lead to severe depression and a lasting psychological effect, resulting in post-traumatic stress such as a fear of future discrimination.
• Feel they are not in control of themselves, leading to high anxiety and constant distress, feeling troubled all the time, which could trigger suicidal tendencies.
• Begin to believe the negative descriptions of themselves and give in to bullying or harassment, thinking they deserve to be treated that way, causing them to doubt and lose faith in themselves.
• Develop a distrust of all people, causing them to isolate themselves and feel disconnected from others, resulting in extreme loneliness.
• Think everyone is rejecting and failing them, which makes them bitter and angry and can lead to revengeful thoughts and actions.
• Feel ashamed at being judged by their association with a group, believing they are not valued or respected as individuals, leading to feelings of inadequacy.
• Start to believe the labelling and act accordingly, feeling helpless and powerless because they think they are not as capable as others.
(2 x 4) (8)
subQuestions.topic: Human factors causing ill health: social factors

subQuestions.questionText: Critically discuss how a person could determine whether he/she may be unintentionally stereotyping others.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award FOUR marks each for TWO well-explained responses (statement + elaborate + qualify + outcome). A person may have to:
• Examine their general approach with others, or ask others to assess it, reflecting on whether they have preconceived ideas of people, which may confirm a narrow-minded attitude and indicate bias or prejudice.
• Do introspection about the group activities they participate in that exclude certain people for unfounded reasons, revealing that they may subconsciously be categorising others.
• Consider their actions towards others and whom they do not associate with, to determine whether they act in discriminatory ways and treat people unfairly.
• Reflect on the movies, books or video games they prefer that promote negative opinions of certain groups, which may imply they are classifying others and following harmful belief systems.
• Think about why they may not support organisations that address stereotypes, which could imply they do not regard stereotyping as wrong and may be prejudiced.
• Make a conscious decision to think about the impact stereotyping has on others, helping them identify situations that affected others negatively and become aware of their own inconsiderate responses.
• Consider whether they are intolerant of people who differ from them or do not share their views, which could make them too critical and indicate being judgemental.
• Reflect on whether they laugh at comments based on stereotypes, which encourages such behaviour and shows their contribution to the problem.
• Monitor their language when talking to different groups to determine whether they use offensive expressions based on generalisations that exclude or disrespect others.
• Question their assumptions based on appearances or someone's background that were reinforced by their own cultural views and influence how they perceive and interact with others.
(2 x 4) (8) [20]
subQuestions.topic: Human factors causing ill health: social factors

questions.title: SECTION C (Answer any TWO of Questions 4, 5 and 6) — Question 5: Entrepreneurship (An innovative strategy to counteract unemployment)
questions.passageText:
ENTREPRENEURSHIP — An innovative strategy to counteract unemployment

Innovation and passion are the heart of entrepreneurship. It is important for entrepreneurs or upcoming entrepreneurs to understand why being innovative and passionate is important and how it may benefit a business. Potential entrepreneurs also need to acquire the mindset of an entrepreneur.

[Adapted from www.igi-global.com. Accessed on 22/03/2023.]

Write paragraphs on entrepreneurship using the three points below as a guideline.

subQuestions.questionText: Briefly state FOUR reasons why entrepreneurs should be innovative.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award ONE mark for each response. It may help them to:
• Find their niche / a gap in the market / access funding.
• Differentiate their business from others offering the same service or product.
• Attract more clients, customers and buyers.
• Improve their chances of staying competitive in the industry.
• Ensure their business can overcome future problems.
• Continue to grow their business in challenging situations.
• Make certain their products or services are original.
• Strive to be inventive and resourceful in their business plans.
• Ensure their business stays relevant in an ever-changing business world.
• Produce advanced products to retain clients.
• Always attempt new business ideas.
• Increase productivity.
(4 x 1) (4)

subQuestions.questionText: Analyse TWO ways in which you could acquire the mindset of an entrepreneur.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award FOUR marks each for TWO well-explained responses (statement + elaborate + qualify + outcome). You could:
• Choose to see challenges as potential opportunities, which encourages you to seek solutions and develop critical thinking skills that teach you how to solve problems as an entrepreneur.
• Accept failure in business as a learning opportunity that teaches resilience and finding your own solutions, opening you to growth so you learn to persevere and improve in future endeavours.
• Develop an opportunity-seeking attitude that drives you to identify your niche, creating a platform to put your business plan into action and take calculated risks.
• Request feedback from clients and employees, helping you understand market needs and improve your service or product for greater business success.
• Build networks with successful entrepreneurs, job-shadow, volunteer, attend seminars and webinars and read about entrepreneurship, helping you learn from others' experiences and stay focused on the key values of entrepreneurship.
• Set a vision for yourself and continuously learn, so you have a clear understanding of your long-term strategies, helping you map your mission and stay on track.
• Learn to be more flexible, adaptable and open to change, so you can easily change your plans when needed and cope better with unexpected challenges without giving up on your goals.
(2 x 4) (8)

subQuestions.questionText: Critically discuss how a young entrepreneur's passion could influence other young people in his/her community to become entrepreneurs.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award FOUR marks each for TWO well-explained responses (statement + elaborate + qualify + outcome). It could:
• Make other young people determined to become enthusiastic about entrepreneurship, driving them towards the actions needed to follow this path and persuading them they could also make it to the top.
• Encourage other young people to develop a strong inner motivation and ambition to be the best at a new venture, showing how nurturing a love for this career helps overcome obstacles.
• Inspire other young people to consider entrepreneurship through the entrepreneur's testimony, influencing them to invest the effort needed and awakening an inner desire to pursue it.
• Attract young people who share the same passion and want to learn from or job-shadow the entrepreneur, building a culture of entrepreneurship among the youth.
• Create ideas for self-employment opportunities in the community, making others aware of their undeveloped potential and persuading them to take the risk, releasing hidden talents and leading to financial freedom.
• Challenge stereotypes that only older people can be entrepreneurs by showcasing their own experience, proving age is not a barrier and encouraging others to challenge conventional norms.
• Share experiences of both successes and failures through campaigns, public speaking, mentorship and social media, providing valuable insights and giving aspiring entrepreneurs confidence.
• Encourage other young people to build networks and communities for entrepreneurs through events and online platforms, connecting like-minded individuals and creating opportunities to learn and find mentors.
• Demonstrate resilience and determination by overcoming barriers and finding innovative solutions, inspiring other young people to tackle their own challenges knowing that passion and dedication can lead to success.
(2 x 4) (8) [20]

questions.title: SECTION C (Answer any TWO of Questions 4, 5 and 6) — Question 6: Responsibility of communities in ensuring safe and healthy living (South Africa's water systems in crisis)
questions.passageText:
RESPONSIBILITY OF COMMUNITIES IN ENSURING SAFE AND HEALTHY LIVING — South Africa's water systems in crisis

Water systems across the country seem not to be effectively maintained, leading to the poor quality of water in most communities. The behaviour of communities has also been found to be one of the contributing factors that lead to water pollution.

Intervention programmes intended to promote safe and healthy living also seem not to be sustainable. Most communities now seek to petition local government for their urgent action in terms of the water crisis.

Glossary: petition — a formal written request, signed by many people, urging authorities in respect of a particular cause.

[Adapted from http://jamiat.org.za. Accessed on 09/01/2023.]

Write paragraphs on the responsibility of communities in ensuring safe and healthy living environments, using the three points below as a guideline.

subQuestions.questionText: Briefly state FOUR advantages of online petitioning to local governments for urgent action in terms of the water crisis in communities.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award ONE mark for each response. Any FOUR of:
• It can be quickly created and launched.
• Faster delivery of the petition.
• Easier tracking of the documents submitted.
• Automatic tracking of the number of signatures / a digital record of signatures as proof.
• A fast, more convenient way of following up on the required actions.
• It lets petitioners keep evidence of documents submitted.
• A more effortless, secure way of holding responsible people accountable.
• It can quickly reach a large group, enabling more people to sign.
• Supporters can sign in their own time and in the privacy of their homes.
• A legitimate paper trail for follow-up that cannot be easily erased or destroyed.
• It helps build momentum and a sense of urgency around the issue.
• It lets concerned citizens quickly and easily spread the word.
• It provides transparency and is open to the public.
(4 x 1) (4)
subQuestions.topic: Communities and safe, healthy living environments

subQuestions.questionText: Analyse TWO ways in which communities could work together with local government to help protect water resources.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award FOUR marks each for TWO well-explained responses (statement + elaborate + qualify + outcome). Communities could:
• Regularly communicate with the municipality and local councillors on social media or at local government meetings to report challenges (leaks, dumping, littering, misuse of water) so these are considered in the maintenance plan and get immediate attention.
• Agree to watch over water preservation in their areas, ensuring officials remain vigilant about maintaining water infrastructure and keeping these resources sustainable and well managed.
• Liaise with local government to participate in voluntary programmes to clean up or recycle water, making the care of water resources everybody's responsibility and supporting local government's efforts.
• Work with local government to develop and enforce bylaws on the safekeeping of water resources, allowing broader community involvement and reinforcing a collective effort to safeguard shared resources.
• Organise educational programmes and awareness campaigns in partnership with local government, focusing on water conservation and changing community attitudes so individuals help preserve water quality and save water.
• Constantly monitor water quality by identifying pollutants, helping local government determine potential sources of pollution and informing more effective maintenance strategies.
• Volunteer to supervise sites during installation or upgrading of water infrastructure and use specialised knowledge, taking ownership of such initiatives and ensuring uninterrupted access to this basic service.
(2 x 4) (8)
subQuestions.topic: Communities and safe, healthy living environments

subQuestions.questionText: Critically discuss TWO ways in which to ensure the sustainability of intervention programmes that intend to promote safe and healthy living.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award FOUR marks each for TWO well-explained responses (statement + elaborate + qualify + outcome). Possible ways:
• Build the capacity of individuals and communities involved by training community members and stakeholders, developing the skills and knowledge needed to keep promoting safe and healthy living even after the programme ends.
• Ensure programmes are adaptable and flexible to respond to changing needs, through regular assessment of relevance, adjusting strategies and impact studies, so they stay effective amid emerging challenges.
• Encourage collaboration among stakeholders and the sharing of knowledge and best practices, benefiting from collective expertise so programmes are continuously supported.
• Hold meetings and implement constant monitoring and evaluation, revealing challenges that can be acted upon to ensure the desired outcomes are achieved.
• Ensure those responsible for implementing activities are committed to their duties, so the programme is carried out as envisaged and no aspect is neglected.
• Secure proper, adequate financial support and ensure funds are properly used, so activities are executed as planned.
• Put appropriate contingency plans in place aligned with possible challenges, so unforeseen matters are dealt with effectively.
• Do proper planning and ensure key role players have the skills to execute the plans, so the objectives and purpose of the intervention are fully achieved.
• Ensure beneficiaries take ownership of and buy into the programme by showing interest and fostering personal responsibility, improving the chances of successful implementation.
(2 x 4) (8) [20]
